A valued client of Edwards & Pearce is seeking an Accounts Administrator to provide additional support to their accounts team. Free parking, family run welcoming company

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
As an Accounts Assistant in Hull, you will help keep the accounting and finance function organised by completing day-to-day finance tasks accurately. Your work will support clear financial records for an organisation in the industrial / manufacturing sector.

Client Details

The organisation operates in the industrial / manufacturing sector in Hull.

Description
- Process day-to-day finance transactions accurately to maintain clear and up-to-date records.
- Enter financial data into internal systems and check information is complete before it is recorded.
- Maintain organised finance files and documents so information is easy to find when needed.
- Review transaction details and resolve basic data queries to reduce errors in financial records.
- Prepare routine finance information for the Accounting & Finance department.
- Work with colleagues to gather documents and information needed for day-to-day finance tasks.
- Keep records accurate and follow agreed internal finance procedures.

Profile

A successful 'Accounts Assistant' should have:
- Experience completing routine finance administration and transaction processing.
- Confidence entering and checking financial data with a high level of accuracy.
- The ability to keep finance documents and records well organised.
- Experience working with finance systems or spreadsheets to maintain clear information.
- The ability to investigate straightforward data queries and correct errors.
- A practical approach to managing day-to-day accounting and finance tasks.

Job Offer
- Temporary, interim Accounts Assistant assignment.
- Location: Hull.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

People are at the heart of Michael Page. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment. As an inclusive recruiter we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and experiences. If you require any adjustments or accommodations during the recruitment process, we'll work with you to ensure you can perform at your best.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Are you an experienced credit controller or accounts assistant with credit control knowledge seeking their next permanent role in Hull? If so, read on

We are currently recruiting for a Credit Controller to join a well-established and growing business based in Hull. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced finance professional who enjoys building strong customer relationships while maintaining effective credit control processes. This role can offer contractual hours of between 37.5 hours and 32.5 hours (pro-rata salary) so could be suitable for someone who wants to work slightly shorter hours.

Working as part of a supportive finance team, you will play a key role in managing customer accounts, reducing aged debt, and ensuring cash flow targets are achieved.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing and maintaining a portfolio of customer accounts
- Proactively chasing outstanding debt via telephone, email, and written correspondence
- Resolving account queries and payment disputes efficiently
- Allocating incoming payments and reconciling customer accounts
- Producing aged debtor reports and highlighting any issues to management
- Supporting month-end processes and finance reporting requirements

About You
- Previous experience within a Credit Controller, Accounts Receivable or Accounts Assistant position
- Strong communication and negotiation skills
- Confident dealing with customers at all levels
- Experience using finance or ERP systems would be advantageous

What's on Offer?
- Salary of £26,000 - £30,000 DOE
- Monday to Friday working hours of 08:30 - 16:30
- Office-based
- Company benefits package
- Ongoing training and development opportunities

Apply today as this role will close soon

title: Facilities Coordinator - 12 Month FTC - Hull
description:
Facilities Coordinator - 12 Month Fixed-Term Contract Location: Hull, East Yorkshire
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Job Type: Full Time 12 Month FTC
Hours: 35 hours per week
Working Pattern: Hybrid / Agile Working
Travel: Regular travel to UK offices, with occasional overnight stays

An excellent opportunity has arisen for a proactive and organised Facilities Coordinator to join the Facilities team of a well-established and forward-thinking legal services organisation based in Hull.

This is a varied and hands-on position, supporting the day-to-day management, maintenance and smooth running of multiple office locations across the UK.

Working closely with colleagues, landlords, contractors and external suppliers, you will help ensure that offices remain safe, compliant, well-maintained and efficient, while supporting facilities projects, office moves and workplace improvements.

Offering hybrid working, an excellent benefits package and exposure to multi-site facilities management, this opportunity would suit someone who enjoys a varied role combining practical problem-solving, facilities administration and health and safety responsibilities.

The Role As Facilities Coordinator, your responsibilities will include:
- Coordinating day-to-day facilities operations, building maintenance and repairs across multiple UK offices.
- Liaising with landlords, maintenance contractors, suppliers and third-party service providers.
- Supporting workplace health and safety compliance, including risk assessments and workstation assessments.
- Monitoring outstanding actions and ensuring facilities and safety issues are addressed promptly.
- Assisting with office moves, refurbishments, minor maintenance works and facilities improvement projects.
- Maintaining accurate facilities records, compliance documentation and building safety information.
- Supporting the review and development of facilities policies, procedures and processes.
- Managing facilities-related requests and tickets through Salesforce.
- Coordinating and booking complex business travel arrangements.
- Supporting internal and external events and ensuring offices operate effectively.

About You We are looking for a practical, organised and approachable individual who enjoys taking ownership of tasks and ensuring things run smoothly.

Essential requirements:
- Previous experience or a good working knowledge of office health and safety procedures.
- IOSH qualification or currently working towards one.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Confident communication skills and the ability to build relationships with colleagues, contractors and suppliers.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
- A proactive, flexible and hands-on approach to problem-solving.
- Ability to work independently and make sound decisions.
- Full UK driving licence and access to a car.
- Willingness to travel regularly between UK offices, including occasional overnight stays.

Desirable experience:
- Previous experience in Facilities Coordination, Facilities Management or Office Management.
- Knowledge of Health and Safety Executive (HSE) guidance.
- First Aid at Work qualification.
- Fire Marshal training or certification.
- Experience supporting multi-site office operations.

Previous experience within a law firm or legal services organisation is not essential.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary, dependent on experience.
- 12-month fixed-term contract.
- Hybrid and agile working arrangements.
- 35-hour working week.
- Private pension.
- Medical insurance.
- Generous annual leave allowance.
- Supportive and collaborative working environment.
- Opportunity to gain experience supporting facilities operations across multiple UK locations.

Interested? If you're an experienced Facilities Coordinator, Facilities Assistant, Office Coordinator or Office Manager with a strong understanding of workplace health and safety, I'd be keen to hear from you.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a progressive organisation offering flexibility, variety and a supportive working environment.

title: Finance Procurement Administrator ( Part-Time)
description:
Who we are

GlobalData operates an intelligence platform that empowers leaders to act decisively in a world of complexity and change.

By uniting proprietary data, human expertise, and purpose-built AI into a single, connected platform, we help organisations see what s coming, move faster, and lead with confidence.

Our solutions are used by over 5,000 organisations across the world s largest industries, delivering tailored intelligence that supports strategic planning, innovation, risk management, and sustainable growth.

Why join GlobalData?

GlobalData is at a pivotal point in its growth journey, and we need curious, ambitious, courageous people to support us in achieving our vision to deliver intelligence that transforms uncertainty into opportunity for the world s most successful organisations.?

Our big ambitions mean that life at GlobalData is fast-paced, entrepreneurial and rewarding. Working together in an intellectually challenging environment, where learning is super-charged to keep us on our toes, the highly stimulating, fast-paced, global environment we operate in, and our bold ambitions result in unique learning opportunities for our people.

The role

We now have an opening for a part- time role(15 hours a week) Procurement Administrator based in Hull. Working within the finance team, we expect you to have close interaction with the wider commercial business, with the main responsibility being processing supplier s invoices and matching to PO s.

Now is an incredibly exciting time to join and be part of a business that is fast-paced, vibrant and ambitious, with opportunities for everyone to develop and succeed.

What you ll be doing
- Matching up incoming supplier invoices to purchase orders in the procurement tracker.
- Submit invoices with 3 way match (PO, Goods Receipt, Invoice) for processing.
- Preparation of payment schedules to deadline.
- Communicate with suppliers to enforce No Po, No Pay policy.
- Query resolution.
- Supplier Statement reconciliations.

What we re looking for
- Technical skills - Knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
- Dedicated and accountable - able to meet deadlines while maintaining strong attention to detail and effectively managing expectations.
- Organised - able to meet deadlines while maintaining strong attention to detail as well as managing expectations effectively.
- A strong communicator - able to communicate well and build strong, collaborative relationships across the business.
- Adaptable and positive mindset - a confident personality with a positive attitude towards change and new challenges.

In addition to a rewarding career, we support our GlobalData colleagues with a range of benefits across health, finances, fitness, travel, tech and more. To find out more about the roles and benefits on offer in your region, visit (url removed)

title: Administrator
company: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
advertiser_name: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
description: Band 2 Administrator Have you ever thought about working for the NHS? Behind every appointment, every clinic, every patient seen - there is someone who made it happen. Our Administrators are the unseen heroes of patient care.They support teams, coordinate workloads, and ensure clinics and departments run safely and efficiently. They are trusted, reliable and central to the smooth delivery of care. Working within fast-paced and supportive teams, you will take on additional responsibility, helping to oversee processes, support colleagues and ensure patients receive the best possible experience. The reassuring voice on the phone. The calm presence supporting patients in what can often be their most worrying moments. Without them, patients don't get seen. Services don't run. Care doesn't flow. You don't need previous NHS experience - we can teach you the systems. What we can't teach is compassion, professionalism and the ability to care about getting things right for patients. That's what we're looking for. What you'll bring: A caring and compassionate approach Confidence communicating with patients and the public Good organisational skills and attention to detail Basic IT skills (typing, email, data entry, use of computer systems) The ability to work as part of a close-knit team Calmness in a sometimes fast-paced environment What you'll gain: The chance to make a real difference every single day Part-time opportunities with flexible working options One of the best pension schemes available Generous annual leave entitlement - because you work hard and deserve proper time off Structured training and ongoing support Genuine career progression - many of our senior leaders began in administrative roles Patient care is at the heart of everything we do, and our administrative teams are central to making that care possible. If you are organised, compassionate, and want a role where your work truly matters, we would love to hear from you. For further details with regard to this vacancy opportunity, please see the attached Job Description and Person Specification. Should we receive a high volume of applications the advert may be closed earlier than stated. Please note that, in line with UKVI regulations, this vacancy does not meet the eligibility criteria for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker Visa route. As a result, we are unable to issue a Certificate of Sponsorship for this position. We remain committed to fair and equal recruitment practices and encourage applications from all suitably qualified candidates who have the right to work in the UK. We are managing the recruitment for this vacancy directly and are not seeking support from recruitment agencies or third-party sourcing providers. We kindly request that agencies do not submit applications, candidate CVs or speculative enquiries in relation to this post. Any unsolicited submissions will not be considered, and no agency fees will be payable unless a formal agreement has been made in advance with the Trust

title: Administration Assistant
description: " Please note that this advertised vacancy does not meet the UKVI eligibility requirements for a Skilled Worker Visa and therefore HTFT would not be able to issue a Certificate of Sponsorship for this role." An opportunity has arisen for a full-time Band 2 Administration Assistant to work within our Mental Health Crisis Team based at Miranda House in Hull. You will be expected to be flexible and work in a fast paced and highly demanding environment within the main office as well as providing cover to a very busy reception area. The administration team provides 24 hour, 7 day a week cover which is worked on a rota basis incorporating enhanced pay for unsocial hours. This provides a refreshing work life balance. This role involves liaising with health care professionals from the Trust and outside agencies, also dealing with queries from patients requiring a service. Excellent interpersonal skills and being able to work on own initiative are both essential. The successful candidate will have good keyboard skills enabling them to assist in creating, developing and maintaining new processes and procedures. This includes regular data inputting using patient systems (Systm One ) in accordance with the Trust standards. Along with all other Microsoft Packages. Applicants will have RSA III and OCRIII/ECDL or equivalent NVQ Qualification, a good standard of Maths and English and have previous experience of carrying out general administrative procedures in an office environment. Experience of using software packages including Microsoft Word/Outlook and Excel are beneficial. Experience with the Trust Patient Information Systems (Systm One ) would be advantageous. For further details with regard to this vacancy opportunity, please see the attached Job Description and Person Specification.
